why_lead: Eve-of-invasion buy-the-dip faith, expressed through the triple-leveraged Nasdaq 100 fund. Significant own-card move: TQQQ 45.14 USD, -7.65% 1-session and -21.22% 5-session, against S&P 500 4,225.50 (-1.84% / -5.49%), Nasdaq 100 13,509.43 (-2.60% / -7.60%), VIX 31.02 (+2.21 pts) and Robinhood -20.56% over five sessions (prior close 2022-02-23). Chronology: the leveraged dip-buy family also ran as smaller items on 2022-02-04 ('the leveraged dip-buy snaps back') and 2022-02-11 ('the dip-buy meets 7.5% inflation'); this is a material update and promotion of the 2022-02-22 secondary item '3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the YOLO dip-buy with triple leverage' (TQQQ then 50.44 USD on the 18 February close). Changed catalyst and reaction: a further 1.84% S&P fall into the correction, Ukraine's state of emergency with the ruble and Russian bonds hammered (n1281), satellite photos of the build-up (n1282) and the separatists' request for Russian military help (n1278). Changed attention, from headlines published after the 22 and 23 February cutoffs: MarketWatch's first-correction-in-two-years 'what history says' piece and bullish-divergence signal (n1908, n1909), Mahaney's post-correction buy list (n1719), UKTN's stocks-to-buy list (n1593), NYT on correction-plus-sanctions (n0640), MarketWatch on Fed speed (n1850). Evidence already used on 22 February (Yahoo YOLO piece, Fortune 'how low', A Wealth of Common Sense, AdvisorHub leveraged-ETF charge, 'peak stupid') and on 23 February (Time's meme-stock lessons, Kiplinger's conflict-and-your-investments guide, Reuters' correction confirmation, CNBC's Dow-low headline) is deliberately not re-cited. Split view: Raymond James (n0445) and MarketWatch's divergence vs Wall St banks' recession fears (n0093), Fed speed (n1850) and the March hike with 50 bps calls (n1801); options expiration (n1571) as positioning risk. Invasion is treated only as a pending risk.
why_smaller: Aerospace & Defense ETF / ITA: material update of the 2022-02-22 secondary item 'Lockheed Martin / LMT — the war trade finally gets its trigger' (the 23 February notes declined a carryover for lack of new defence evidence). New evidence published 23 February: the FT reports ETF investors piling into Russian equities and defence stocks (n0837), adding the 'buy the target' Russia leg: Russian markets pared a plunge (n1245), Market Realist's who-owns-Lukoil explainer (n0782), ruble and bonds hit (n1281), Buffett avoids Russia (n0658). Card: LMT 388.90 USD +0.70% / +1.75% 5-session, GD +1.64% 5-session vs S&P -5.49%, while ITA fell 1.14% to 101.69 USD (-3.98% 5-session) and RTX/NOC fell. The Sberbank/VTB rebound used on 23 February is not re-cited.

Palantir Technologies / PLTR: material update of the 2022-02-18 lead 'Palantir Technologies / PLTR — the growth bill hits the faithful' (the Reuters margin-hit headline, PLTR 11.77 USD). New angle and evidence published 22 February: Karp's 'bad times are good for Palantir' alongside increased losses and a tumbling share price (Diginomica n0558), recast as a war-tech faith trade on the eve of a possible invasion, and the CDC contract (Reuters n0564); card shows a further slide to 10.43 USD, -26.39% 5-session, -20.14% 20-session from 13.06 USD, with the 2Y up 56 bps over 20 observations. Kept secondary; the 18 February margin headline is not re-cited.

Wheat / ZW=F: a distinct food-inflation war premium. The 2022-02-23 Brent lead folded wheat into its commodity spillover (+5.93% to 844.25 US cents/bu); this standalone item rests on newly published 23 February evidence: CNBC's breadbasket explainer (n1703), Successful Farming's Wednesday close (n1714), Bloomberg's fertilizer warning with Mosaic +2.29% (n0715), plus Reuters on curbed food supplies (n0571); card 876.00 US cents/bu, +3.76% 1-session, +12.34% 5-session, corn +7.17%, soybeans +7.98% 5-session.
considered_not_chosen: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (88.50 USD, -4.74% 1-session; Washington Post 'disastrous launch' n1595, WTR EU hurdle n1596): DWAC led on 21 and 22 February and was a smaller item on 23 February (surge, Apptopia downloads, 13-hour crash); a fourth consecutive appearance on one red session and one new verdict was not justified.

Gold / GC=F and GDX vs bitcoin (CNBC 'digital gold is falling apart', n0848; gold 1,910.40 USD/oz +2.92% 5-session, GDX +6.93%, BTC 37,296.57 USD -6.83% 5-session): prices barely changed since the 2022-02-21 Bitcoin and GDX items and gold was also a 2022-02-14 item; one new CNBC headline did not justify a third version.
ARK Innovation ETF / ARKK (60.88 USD, -19.13% 5-session; Cathie Wood 'way undervalued' n1516, misallocation n1532): the same buy-the-dip faith as the TQQQ lead, and ARKK already ran on 2022-02-01.
Brent and oil ETFs (Brent 96.84 USD, +0.00% on the session; Seeking Alpha oil ETFs n1150): the 2022-02-23 lead, with no material change.

Block / SQ and Coinbase Global / COIN into results (SQ 88.72 USD -22.99% 5-session, Investopedia preview n0685; COIN 172.74 USD -17.33% 5-session): pending results only; a preview cannot carry a crowd story.

Lucid Group / LCID (23.97 USD, -6.04% 1-session; recall headlines n0669, n1709): its results fell after the 23 February close with no eligible outcome headline, so any item would have been stale or speculative.

Ford Motor / F EV-split story (2022-02-22 smaller item): Ford's CEO has since said there are no plans to spin off the EV business (Reuters n0976), but no retail-attention evidence or card catalyst justified revisiting it.
Vertiv / VRT (-36.74% 1-session), Airbnb / ABNB (-9.20%), HIMS (+13.10%), DraftKings (+5.59%): large moves without an explaining own-date headline or crowd narrative.

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff: n0135 (Reuters 'Expert views on Russian forces invading Ukraine', stamped 23 February but describing the invasion), n1265 (excluded), n0753 (NYT 'Russia-Ukraine crisis shakes markets, but long-term outlook is better', publication time uncertain).
